# Frozen Legacy Observations

Rust tests read these data files directly. No Python interpreter, OpenCV process or automatic expectation generator is called. The application and Windows package do not consume or include this directory.

`provenance.json` pins the application baseline `cde68bc2eb1285eddcd8a261cdfe411ed4924f76`, the separately preserved oracle/tool reference `d11737aeb6ec885293b2f6c0e01e9f44aad0ba15`, source hashes/Git blobs, the 76 application-file responsibility mappings, Python3.7.9/OpenCV4.13.0/NumPy1.21.6 observation environment and generated Rust table provenance. The source/tool code is available in Git history only. `input-files.json` records the approved asset/config state during observation, including documentation for inventory; it is historical evidence, not a requirement that every document stay byte-identical.

`manifest.json` lists the exact compressed cases and their sizes/SHA256. Each `<family>/<identity>.json.gz` contains an independently observed `expected` JSON value and `identity_sha256`. The identity hashes the normalized request plus the referenced input files. Configuration directory inputs include JSON files only and retain object insertion order. Other file/bank inputs retain their bytes; JSON uses parsed content with normalized paths. Test-generated AVI files and Rust calibration/overlay outputs are included in that identity, so changed output cannot reuse an unrelated old decode/pixel-comparison result. Implicit shared assets also remain traceable through the input inventory and the Rust tests' actual loaders.

The stateful town bridge also binds existing `--state` JSON. Its next reference state comes from the previous **independent observation**, not the current Rust result. One observation's identity was strengthened after review to include that before-state; `identity_rebindings` records both identities, the prior observation and the unchanged expected-value hash. Source SHA256 values describe the pre-removal working files; Git blob IDs also identify the normalized historical content when line endings differ.

Tests declare indirect files with `paths`: saved reports and sidecar frames, original/decoded JPEG images and the town/automap manifest/template banks. Four initially incomplete identities were independently re-observed using the pinned source and the same recorded OpenCV build; all parsed expected values matched the earlier observations. The temporary reference code/packages were removed again. `independent_refresh` records this evidence. Superseded unused cases were pruned; old identity strings are provenance identifiers, not promises that obsolete lookup files remain available.

Checkout and per-test temporary owners use reversible path markers. Literal marker spellings and error-message backslash representations round-trip without changing the test value. The reader bounds compressed and decoded data to64MiB each and rejects invalid/truncated/trailing data, a missing case or missing expected field. It does not silently fall back to current Rust output. The fixture helper refuses ambiguous checkout-root config inputs; this does not change the application's config loader. `tests/rust-legacy-baseline.rs` checks these boundaries, generated-table/inventory hashes and the absence of project Python code/environments.

The observations preserve the selected cases, not an exhaustive proof of all behavior. Recording tests reuse independent decode/seek/quality results only for the exact newly generated AVI bytes. They do **not** run a fresh independent MPEG-4 decoder on every future bitstream. A changed codec/output needs a separately reviewed independent decode and new evidence. Time measurements in old observations do not establish current performance; live evidence remains in its owning evaluation.

Run `cargo test --all-targets --locked` for current regression. New cases or intentional behavior changes require independently reviewed expectations and an updated provenance/inventory. Do not derive the expected value from the implementation under test or merely rename an existing fixture to satisfy a new key. The retired one-time Python generators are represented by frozen Rust Unicode11/drawing/VLC data, source fingerprints and retained notices; a general upstream/Unicode-version regeneration tool is not provided.

For bounded fixture maintenance, `D2BOT_BASELINE_COVERAGE_DIR` can name a task-owned output directory. The Rust reader writes empty `<family>/<identity>.seen` receipts for actually used cases, without modifying expected values. Remove those receipts after reviewing/pruning the inventory. The [retirement run](../../../docs/plans/run/run-20261031-01-rust-source-retirement.md) owns this session's checks and [merge check](../../../docs/plans/refactoring/refactor-0002-rust-port-merge-check.md) owns parity limits.
